LESSON: TIME (DAILY ROUTINES)

Grade: SNE  /  physical-impairment / PP1
Subject: General
Strand: Measurement 3.3 Capacity (how much a container can hold) (10 lessons) By the end
Topic 3.4: Time (Daily Routines)
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 10

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Time (Daily Routines), part of Measurement 3.3 Capacity (how much a container can hold) (10 lessons) By the end in SNE  /  physical-impairment / PP1 General.

Key inquiry question: Why do we use time in our day to day activities?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

Refer to the KICD curriculum reference at the end of this lesson for the full list of outcomes.

SECTION 3: KEY CONCEPTS AND EXPLANATION

A. Suggested learning experiences (from KICD)

1. Talk about four daily routine activities done at home before going to school. Learners with speech difficulties could use other alternative modes of communication to share their responses

2. Talk about four activities related to time.

3. Arrange four pictures of activities done every day.

4. Work with others in purposive groups/pairs to arrange four pictures of activities done every day, Learners with manipulation difficulties could use alternative functional parts of the body or appropriate assistive devices to perform given tasks.

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

1. Talk about four daily routine activities done at home before going to school. Learners with speech difficulties could use other alternative modes of communication to share their responses
2. Talk about four activities related to time.
3. Arrange four pictures of activities done every day.
4. Work with others in purposive groups/pairs to arrange four pictures of activities done every day, Learners with manipulation difficulties could use alternative functional parts of the body or appropriate assistive devices to perform given tasks.

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Time (Daily Routines) together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Core Competencies to be developed:
Communication and collaboration: learners talk to and work with each other as they arrange pictures of various daily activities.

Values:
Respect: learners take turns to arrange pictures of different daily activities in sequence.

Pertinent and Contemporary Issues:
(PCIs):

Safety: learners sing songs on the need of not to be late for home.

Link to Other Activity Areas:

The learner is able to relate arranging of pictures on daily activities in sequence to pre-writing skills in Language Activities.
